universe: same static 35-symbol canonical universe used throughout this entire research program (talonx_piv.config.DEFAULT_UNIVERSE)

listing_date_check.method: Reasoned from general knowledge of each company's public-listing history (no corporate-actions/listing-date data source exists in this repo to query programmatically) -- flagged as NOT independently verified against a data source, only against general knowledge.
listing_date_check.conclusion: All 35 symbols were large, publicly-listed, liquid mega/large-cap names throughout the entire 2024-2026 research horizon used by this program. The most recently listed among them (PYPL, spun off from eBay in 2015; AVGO's current corporate form dates to 2016; PANW listed 2012) all predate 2024 by nearly a decade or more. No IPO/listing-date gap exists for any symbol within any period this program has used or plans to use.

corporate_actions_check.method: Not independently verified against a splits/dividends data source -- none exists in this repo. Bars are downloaded with adjustment=raw (unadjusted).
corporate_actions_check.known_risk: A material stock split within any DEVELOPMENT/VALIDATION/REPLICATION window would appear as a single-bar price discontinuity, which check_data_quality's invalid_ohlc_relationship/invalid_prices checks would NOT necessarily catch (a 4-for-1 split still produces valid, positive, correctly-ordered OHLC, just at a different scale) -- this is a genuine blind spot.
corporate_actions_check.mitigation: None applied -- documented honestly rather than fabricating a corporate-actions calendar. If a future task adds a splits data source, it should re-check all periods this program has used.
corporate_actions_check.residual_risk_classification: UNRESOLVED_DATA_INTEGRITY_CAVEAT -- not fabricated away, carried forward in task71_summary.md.

current_universe_backcast_bias.explanation: The 35-symbol universe is TODAY's liquid, large/mega-cap set (Nasdaq-100-adjacent), applied retroactively to 2024-2026 history. No historical index-constituent reconstruction was attempted -- doing so would require a historical-membership data source this repo does not have, and fabricating one would be worse than acknowledging the gap. This means: (a) any symbol that would have been dropped from a liquid/mega-cap universe during 2024-2026 due to underperformance is NOT in this universe and never was tested -- a form of survivorship bias favoring names that stayed large/liquid; (b) conversely, no symbol that entered mega-cap status only recently is included either (the set is static, not point-in-time). This does NOT necessarily invalidate the research -- the goal is currently-tradeable liquid names for an eventual PAPER/live universe, not a historically representative sample -- but it DOES mean any 'this effect exists across the market' claim should be read as 'this effect exists across today's liquid mega-cap set,' not a market-wide claim.
current_universe_backcast_bias.confidence_impact: Recorded as a confidence caveat on any Task71 candidate nomination, not a disqualifying defect.

sector_concentration.method: Manual sector tagging (no sector-classification data source in this repo -- reasoned from general knowledge).
sector_concentration.conclusion: Roughly 19-20 of 35 symbols (>50%) are technology/semiconductor names -- a material sector concentration. Any cross-sectional finding (e.g. 'top1_symbol_contribution <=40%') can still mask a SECTOR-level concentration if the effect is really a tech/semi-sector phenomenon expressed across many correlated names, not a genuinely idiosyncratic one. This is exactly why Family C (residual momentum) computes a market-model residual (vs SPY) -- controlling for at least the market-wide component -- though a sector-level control (vs. XLK) was not built out in Task71 due to time/scope, and is recorded as a residual limitation.
